newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori calls for "calm" in Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori calls for "calm" in Ecuador.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori voiced "deep concern" about the constitutional crisis in neighbouring Ecuador and said he accepted its request to postpone talks over their border dispute.

"The Peruvian government, in solidarity with its brother country Ecuador, prays for calm in these difficult moments to reach a solution to this crisis," Fujimori told local radio late on Friday before leaving for a working visit to London.

The Peruvian leader said the crisis that began on Thursday when Ecuador's Congress ousted President Abdala Bucaram and replaced him with Speaker Fabian Alarcon "has endangered the stability of the government of President Abdala Bucaram."
A flamboyant populist who faced a nationwide strike this week against his unpopular austerity measures, Bucaram has refused to step down.
His vice president, Rosalia Arteaga, issued a decree appointing herself president and Bucaram's loyal defence minister declared a nationwide state of emergency.

Fujimori said he had received a request from what he referred to as "the government of President Abdala Bucaram" to postpone Feb. 17 talks in Brazil aimed at resolving a 55-year- old border dispute between the two Andean neighbours.

The dispute erupted into a brief but bloody border war in early 1995 that left dozens killed and hundreds injured on both sides. The talks were due to take place in Brasilia, where a peace treaty ending the border conflict was signed two years ago.
"Peru has accepted this request, with the hope of a quick solution to the difficulties Ecuador is passing through, so that a new date can be set," Fujimori said.
Fujimori and Bucaram hugged each other at historic talks in Lima in mid-January and made effusive pledges to strive to overcome their border dispute.

"In the last few months, we have made substantive advances to talk about our disagreements," Fujimori said on Friday. "We don't want these advances to be interrupted or threatened. For that reason, we reiterate our firm will to continue moving forward."

According to government and military sources, Peruvian forces began mobilising along the border with Ecuador in response to concerns about the turmoil engulfing its northern neighbour following Bucaram's ouster.
